title: ops-reliability-1to1-scratchpad-2026-03-20
content:
Purpose: prep notes for weekly SRE ops sync + one-on-one with Jonas (onboarding check / incident followups). Quick, rough — longitudinal view + questions to raise.

Top-level agenda for 1:1 (30m):
- 5m: quick check-in (how's onboarding, blockers)
- 10m: review last week's pages / SLO deviations, decide follow-ups
- 10m: incident triage ownership + capacity plans for next sprint
- 5m: AOB + next steps

Notes to self / talking points:
- Onboarding: Jonas ramp looks good; still fuzzy on our alerting playbooks (need to pair him with Priya on runbook edits).
- Remind to ask about his confidence with PagerDuty rotations and escalation matrix.
- Confirm he has access to private deploy logs and the long-retention S3 bucket.

SLO snapshot (last 7d): (quick numbers to read aloud)
- API request latency P95 (production): 410ms (target <= 300ms) => 2.3% error budget burn this window
- Token-generation throughput tail: 6.8k tok/s sustained on dcap pool (expected 8k) => intermittent CPU throttling, correlates with nightly batch jobs
- Inference error rate (5xx): 0.9% (target <= 0.2%) => spike on 2026-03-16 tied to model cold-start regression
- Pager volume: 28 pages (week) vs baseline 12 (big jump)

Initial hypotheses for pages spike:
1) Model rollout triggered mismatch in compat layer (automatic fallback loop created repeated errors) — see JIRA-OPS-8721 for trace.
2) Nightly cache purge + high concurrent short-lived requests caused KV cache churn and elevated latencies.
3) New customer traffic pattern (enterprise X) hit un-quantized model variant causing memory pressure.

What to bring up in sync:
- Short-term mitigations implemented: pinned previous model version in routing (reduce failure rate), extended KV cache TTLs for high QPS routes, temp scaling bump for dcap pool overnight. Note: need to propose permanent fix (see action items).
- Question for platform-eng: is there an automated check we can add to rollout pipeline to detect infinite fallback loops? (owner: Priya)
- Ask infra: can we move nightly batch windows to 02:00 UTC to avoid peak for APAC customers? (owner: Jonas to coordinate with infra)

Top incidents this week (concise summaries):
- Incident I-2026-03-16-A: "Generation 5xx surge during model rollout"
  - Impact: ~18% of requests for 45 minutes returned 5xx; multiple customer alerts; two P1 pages
  - Root cause (current hypothesis): compatibility mismatch between newest tokenizer binary and older runtime kernels causing invalid request path -> fallback loop
  - Mitigation: rolled back model variant in routing; applied hotfix to detect and short-circuit fallback; created JIRA-OPS-8721 to track permanent fix
  - Follow-ups: add rollout gate (smoke tests + canary to 2% traffic), add regression test to eval suite for tokenizer/runtime combinations

- Incident I-2026-03-18-B: "KV cache thrash leading to tail latency"
  - Impact: P95 jump from 280ms -> 520ms for 30m window on dedicated pool; pages to oncall
  - Root cause: cache TTL default lowered in previous PR; combined with bursting traffic, resulted in many cold starts and higher KV sync load
  - Mitigation: restored TTL, warmed cache for high-QPS routes, queued longer pre-warm for midnight jobs
  - Follow-ups: review PR that lowered TTL (PR#3412), add metric for cache churn rate and alert if > X/min

Paging trends (observed):
- More noise from integration errors (third-party vendor timeouts) — approx 40% of pages are integration-related; need partner SRE contact list
- Rising alert fatigue: same 6 alerts flip 3–4 times/week; we should evaluate combined alert rollout and severity tuning

Immediate action items (who/when):
- Morgan: write post-incident draft for I-2026-03-16-A (status: draft) and share in #sre-retros for comments (due: 2026-03-21)
- Jonas: coordinate with infra to propose shifted batch window and report back (due: 2026-03-22)
- Priya: implement rollout gate in pipeline (canary + smoke) and add simple rollback automation (due: 2026-03-28)
- Platform-eng (nominate): add fallback-loop detector in runtime (proposal by 2026-04-02)
- Observability: create cache-churn metric & dashboard (owner: observability eng, assign ticket CONFLUENCE-1234) (due: 2026-03-26)
- Oncall docs: update runbook "model-rollouts" to include gating checklist + rollback steps (owner: Morgan + Priya) (due: 2026-03-24)

Low-effort wins to propose in sync:
- Add a brief canary-sample smoke test that runs a small token-generation on every rollout (5s) — lightweight, immediate guard 
- Deduplicate integration-timeout alerts into single composite symptom (reduce noise)
- Short note to product: ask enterprise-sdks team to notify SRE 24h before large customer traffic migrations

Questions for Jonas / to raise in 1:1:
- Which runbook sections are unclear? Where should we focus onboarding pairing?
- Any friction with PD rotations or alert ownership?
- Do you have bandwidth to take the cache-churn dashboard ticket next week?

Follow-up cadence and next meeting notes:
- Weekly ops sync: Thu 10:00 PT — cover SLOs, open incidents, paging trends, progress on action items
- Postmortem cadence: aim for draft within 48h of incident, final within 2 weeks; check enforcement of these timelines in the repo

Notes-to-self (small checklist):
- [ ] Draft postmortem I-2026-03-16-A (start with timeline + key logs)
- [ ] Confirm test coverage for tokenizer/runtime combos (ask Research/Applied ML)
- [ ] Add brief to next eng-all-hands about rollout best-practices (5m)
- [ ] Revisit alert thresholds for integration-timeouts (meet with partner ops)

Freeform brain-dump (for later organization):
- Could we implement a "fallback budget" concept: if fallback count > X in Y minutes, automatically pause rollout and notify oncall with actionable pointers? Specs needed.
- Consider adding a per-deployment chaos window to ensure cold-starts are exercised in staging prior to GA rollouts.
- Revisit dedicated pool autoscaling policy: current step-scaling isn't fast enough for bursty enterprise traffic (proposal: move to predictive scaling for known customers with scheduled exports).

End of scratchpad. Will tidy into a formal agenda + share with crew before Thu sync.

-- Morgan
